checks: Dropping the harness reply to the real realbud_require_portal_person RPC (single-use fault injection) makes /account fail closed with a plain sentence and no status code, then a normal request right after succeeds again.
AI usage & billing serves a skeleton, a visually hidden loading label and aria-busy in its first HTML, before any client fetch resolves.
The overview care fee is never the literal $125.00 fallback: with no agreed fee in the fixture, it reads "On your invoice", not a fabricated amount.
None of the five billing-group pages renders a bare failure code or an "Oops" in its server HTML.

Overview, AI usage & billing, invoices, rates and limits render at 360, 768, 1280 px in light and at 1280 px in dark with no horizontal overflow, and every rendered .notice carries no HTTP status digits.

layers.portal: actual built Next pages, cookies and APIs rendered in Chromium
layers.database: actual disposable PostgreSQL RPCs, including one single-use dropped-reply fault injection
layers.gateway: none: this harness serves no managed-gateway (/v1/portal/*) or platform-billing transport

limits: No deployed site, real customer account or real provider sign-in.

The managed gateway and platform billing are not served by this harness, so every one of the five pages renders its unreachable/unconfigured failure branch here, never a loaded or empty payload. Those shapes are unit-tested in lib/portal-errors.test.mjs, lib/platform-billing.test.mjs and lib/platform-analytics.test.mjs. Serving them here would require adding /v1/portal/* and platform-billing routes to scripts/testing/command-site.mjs, which is outside this packet's file ownership.
The skeleton-before-load assertion applies only to AI usage & billing (a client component); the other four pages are server components with no separate loading state to assert.
